note: Realistic filled-in states in the scoring engine's shape. `expected` is computed by `bin/test-personas --update` and verified by `bin/test-personas`. `hasCriticalFinding` covers only cord/cauda-equina compression, haemorrhage, and infarct — a large lesion (>= 30mm) is its own dedicated major-severity trigger (R-SEV-MAJOR-02), entirely separate from the critical-classification predicate, so a large but non-compressive mass escalates only to 'urgent' follow-up, not 'critical-alert'. The second persona below isolates exactly that distinction.

personas.name: normal-brain-mri-complete
personas.description: A normal brain MRI for chronic headache with no red-flag features: normal parenchyma, ventricles, and posterior fossa, no structural abnormality, every mandatory report section present — expect normal classification + none severity + 100% completeness + routine follow-up + no-action.

state.impression: Normal brain MRI; no structural abnormality identified.

personas.name: abnormal-large-meningioma-major-not-critical-complete
personas.description: A contrast-enhanced brain MRI for new headache and mild weakness shows a large (34mm) right frontal convexity meningioma with a dural tail and mild vasogenic oedema, but no haemorrhage, infarct, or cord involvement: the 30mm large-lesion threshold (R-SEV-MAJOR-02) is a dedicated severity trigger entirely separate from `hasCriticalFinding` (cord compression, haemorrhage, infarct), so this grades major severity but escalates only to 'urgent' follow-up, never critical-alert; report complete — expect abnormal classification + major severity (reportingCategory large-lesion) + 100% completeness + urgent follow-up + specialist-referral.

state.sequencesPerformed: T1, T1 post-contrast, T2, FLAIR axial and coronal sequences.
state.clinicalHistory: New-onset headache and mild left-sided weakness; MRI brain with contrast to investigate.
state.comparisonWithPrevious: No previous brain MRI on file.
state.findingsNarrative: A large, well-circumscribed, homogeneously enhancing extra-axial mass measuring 34mm is seen over the right frontal convexity, with a dural tail, in keeping with a meningioma. Mild surrounding vasogenic oedema. No haemorrhage, infarct, or cord compression.
state.recommendedFollowUp: Refer to neurosurgery for consideration of resection given the size and mass effect.

expected.recommendedAction: Arrange urgent clinical review and expedite onward referral.

personas.name: critical-cervical-cord-compression-uncommunicated-incomplete
personas.description: A cervical spine MRI shows a large central C5/C6 disc herniation causing severe canal stenosis with cord compression and abnormal T2 cord signal, in keeping with early myelopathy: cord compression is a critical structured finding that auto-escalates classification to critical and follow-up to critical-alert regardless of the other axes; the result has not yet been recorded as communicated, no originating request is linked, and the clinical history, comparison, and impression sections are not yet completed while urgent spinal surgical assessment is arranged — expect critical classification + major severity + 40% completeness + critical-alert follow-up + urgent-review.

state.sequencesPerformed: T1, T2 sagittal and axial sequences of the cervical spine.
state.findingsNarrative: A large central disc herniation at C5/C6 is causing severe spinal canal stenosis with cord compression and abnormal T2 cord signal at this level, in keeping with early myelopathy.
state.clinicianNotes: Phoned through to the on-call spinal surgery team immediately; patient being urgently assessed for decompressive surgery.

expected.recommendedAction: Communicate the critical result directly to the referrer now and document the conversation.
